title: Dark Fantasy
paragraphs: An early-1940s supernatural anthology of ghosts, curses, strange legends, and psychological horror, written and produced for radio by Scott Bishop.

Horror/suspense anthology written by Scott Bishop, originating at WKY Oklahoma City and moving to NBC network presentation in January 1942. RadioGOLDINdex disagrees with the specialist log on the program number of the May 1, 1942 broadcast.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: WKY local era (November 14, 1941 to December 26, 1941) and NBC network era (January 2, 1942 to June 19, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Scott Bishop (writer, director, and host), Ben Morris (performer), Tom Paxton (announcer), Eleanor Naylor Caughron (performer), Muir Hite (performer), Fred Wayne (performer), and Garland Moss (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.94ffaea84a0018ac|WKY]].

The stories often return to horror and supernatural threat, suspense and mortal danger, death, murder and the dead, curses, superstition and occult belief, sea, ships and maritime mystery, and past, time and historical intrusion.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes WKY local horror anthology, NBC network transition, Sustaining network horror, and Incomplete survival of a 31-program run.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|pat-novak-for-hire|Pat Novak, for Hire]] and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]].
